## [20] Towards acoustic connectivity corridors?
<hr />

{{< fa calendar-days >}}&nbsp; October 2026
<br/>{{< fa user >}}&nbsp; **Jean-Yves Barnagaud** (CNRS-CEFE, France) 
<br/>{{< fa globe >}}&nbsp; [ACOUCENE](https://www.fondationbiodiversite.fr/en/the-frb-in-action/programs-and-projects/le-cesab/acoucene/) project

<br/>

**Abstract**

The information flow circulating within ecosystems underpins a network of 
semiotic connectivity that contributes to biodiversity dynamics at the landscape 
and local scales. Public environmental policies are beginning to take this 
informational dimension into account. It remains, however, difficult to 
characterize. Acoustics is likely the most measurable vector of information and 
has the advantage of being easy for stakeholders to understand. This likely 
explains the rise of the concept of soundscapes and the scientific discipline 
that studies them, ecoacoustics. While indicators of soundscapes dynamics are 
now operational, their relationship to the processes that enable acoustic 
connectivity in landscapes has yet to be established. Acoucène offers an initial 
approach toward this goal, combining empirical research with the development of 
a theoretical framework, using common passerines in metropolitan France as a 
case study. This seminar details the project’s approach, the theoretical and 
methodological challenges, and prospects for operationalizing the concept of 
acoustic connectivity in the context of spatial planning strategies based on 
ecological corridors.
